scientific_question: What is the shortest causal history of realized dense Muon c_proj updates that remains aligned with the future phase chord?

trajectory.execution: Y400 foreground runner in one tmux session, direct operator polling, no watchdog, callback, queue, heartbeat, or PRO6

diagnostic.full_chord_metric: squared cosine of cumulative early displacement and optimal capture by the span of individual early updates
diagnostic.causal_metric: squared cosine of cumulative early displacement against the future-only chord W_end-W_start+h and optimal capture of that future-only chord by the early-update span
diagnostic.autocorrelation: cosine of update h with update 1 and update h-1

decision_rule.instantaneous_direction_supported: horizon-1 future capture >= 0.50 with positive cosine in every phase/layer cell
decision_rule.compact_history_supported: select the shortest horizon <=12 whose energy-weighted future-span capture is >=0.50, whose cumulative future cosine is positive in every cell, and whose minimum cell future-span capture is >=0.20
decision_rule.no_short_history: if no horizon qualifies, do not implement a static or short-history c_proj chart; capture raw gradients/optimizer state or move to activation-conditioned structure

caveats: Realized updates contain momentum, weight decay, stochastic batches, and the learning-rate schedule.
History-span capture is an in-sample local direction diagnostic and does not itself define a deployable parameterization.
The replay is one short optimizer trajectory, not a global solution-manifold estimate.
